title: Composite-target scaling governor: safe multi-metric autoscaling policy and runtime controls
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding unsafe surge behavior and noisy oscillation. Current autoscalers rely on single-signal heuristics (p95 latency or token throughput) which either overprovision or fail to respect tenant isolation and burst budgets. Goal: design and implement a composable autoscaling governor that evaluates multiple target metrics, applies conservative control logic with explicit safety fences, and exposes runtime controls for fleet operators and product rollouts.

Proposed approach:
1) Composite target metrics: define a weighted composite score composed of (a) per-tenant throughput saturation (tokens/s relative to committed capacity), (b) p95/p99 latency headroom for tail-sensitive workloads, (c) GPU occupancy and kv-cache hit rate for memory-sensitive models, and (d) queue depth and RPS for short requests. Each metric normalized to 0..1 and expressed with a confidence window (decay/exponential smoothing).

2) Multi-algorithm scaling pipeline: implement a two-stage controller: a predictive warmup stage (lightweight time-series forecasting + short-horizon ML model) to request proactive capacity during predictable demand ramps; and a conservative closed-loop stage (PID-derived proportional+derivative with quantile targeting) to make incremental adjustments against the composite score. The closed-loop stage enforces min-step and max-step limits.

3) Safety limits and fences: slope limit (max % change per 5m), surge budget ledger (per-tenant and fleet-level credits), minimum committed baseline (never scale below reserved throughput), and emergency kill-switch that falls back to lower-cost model variants or throttles non-critical tenants. Include rollback triggers when error rates or eviction counts exceed thresholds.

4) Policy DSL and templating: a compact policy spec that lets operators pick target composition, algorithm parameters (PID gains, forecast horizon), and safety envelopes. Provide policy presets: "conservative-stability", "balanced-latency", "aggressive-burst". Policies discoverable in Console with preview simulations.

5) Observability and verification: new telemetry streams (composite_score, predicted_headroom, step_recommendation, applied_delta) emitted with each decision. Dashboards: per-fleet and per-tenant views, histograms for step sizes, and heatmaps for policy activation. Add an offline simulator to replay traces (synthetic + past production) and compute safety metrics (SLA breach probability, cost delta, oscillation index).

6) Rollout plan: start with read-only decision recommendations for a set of staging fleets, then opt-in closed-loop for low-risk tenants, followed by gradual expansion with automatic rollback on safety violations.

Success criteria: reduces p95 SLA breaches by >= 30% for bursty workloads while keeping committed-capacity overage cost within 12% compared to baseline; no repeatable oscillations observed in 30-day replay tests.

Risks & mitigations: forecast model mispredictions -> cap predictive budget and require warmup confirmations; configuration complexity -> provide sane presets and safe defaults; multi-tenant fairness -> enforce per-tenant surge budgets and enforcement layer in the routing tier.

Deliverables: policy spec + schema, runtime controller implementation (predictive + closed-loop), simulator and test harness, Console integration (policy editor + telemetry), rollout playbook and runbook.
